heroIntro: For overseas Bangladeshi parents, grandparents, and siblings residing in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, or Australia, transferring real estate assets, flats, or ancestral land in Bangladesh to children or close relatives is most efficiently executed through a **Heba Deed (হেবা দলিল - Gift Deed under Muslim Law)**. Unlike general sale deeds (সাফ কবলা দলিল) which attract substantial registration fees, local transfer taxes, and source taxes (up to 8-10% of property valuation), a Heba among eligible blood relatives enjoys immense statutory tax exemptions, requiring only a nominal fixed stamp duty of BDT 100. Understanding how to execute a Heba from abroad saves thousands of dollars and guarantees ironclad title transfer.

quickAnswer.heading: Heba Deed from Abroad: Essential Facts
points: Under Section 17(1) of the Registration Act 1908, every gift of immovable property under Muslim law must be executed by a registered written deed.
Heba between 33 designated blood relations incurs only a nominal fixed Stamp Duty of BDT 100 (plus minimal registration and local government fees).
Three theological and legal essentials: Declaration of gift (Ijab) by donor, Acceptance (Qubul) by donee, and Delivery of possession.
Overseas donors can execute a Special Power of Attorney abroad authorizing a representative to sign the Heba deed before the Sub-Registrar in Bangladesh.
Heba-bil-Ewaz (gift with consideration) requires proof of reciprocal exchange and follows different fiscal rules.
Immediately following registration, an e-Namjari mutation must be completed in the donee's name.

sections.h2: The Three Essentials of a Valid Heba Under Muslim Law
sections.content:
Under Islamic jurisprudence and Bangladeshi property law, a Heba requires three foundational legal components:

  1. Declaration of Gift (ইজাব / Ijab): An unequivocal, voluntary statement by the donor (দাতা) expressing an intention to divest ownership without coercion.
  2. Acceptance of Gift (কবুল / Qubul): Acceptance by the donee (গ্রহীতা), either expressly or impliedly. In the case of a minor child, acceptance is made by the legal guardian.
  3. Delivery of Possession (দখল অর্পণ): Handing over actual physical or constructive possession of the subject property to the donee.

sections.h2: Mandatory Registration Requirement: Section 17 Registration Act 1908
sections.content:
Historically, oral gifts under Islamic law were recognized in Bengal. However, following the Law Reforms Ordinance 2004 amending Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908:

All gifts of immovable property (Heba) under Muslim law must be made by a registered instrument. An unregistered oral Heba has zero legal validity in Bangladesh and cannot be used to effect mutation or defend title in court.

sections.h2: The 33 Eligible Blood Relations for Nominal BDT 100 Stamp Duty
sections.content:
The government of Bangladesh provides extraordinary stamp duty relief for gifts among 33 specific degrees of blood relationships under the Finance Act and Stamp Act 1899:

  • Husband and Wife (স্বামী-স্ত্রী)
  • Father / Mother to Son / Daughter (পিতা-মাতা ও সন্তান)
  • Grandfather / Grandmother to Grandson / Granddaughter (দাদা-দাদী, নানা-নানী ও নাতি-নাতনী)
  • Full Brothers and Sisters (সহোদর ভাই-বোন)
  • Paternal / Maternal Uncles/Aunts and Nephews/Nieces under specific statutory definitions

If the gift is made within these 33 categories, the stamp duty is fixed at just BDT 100, exempting the parties from ad-valorem stamp duty (which is otherwise 1.5% - 3%).

sections.h2: Difference Between Simple Heba and Heba-bil-Ewaz
sections.content:
Expatriates must avoid confusing these two distinct legal instruments:

  • Simple Heba (হেবা): A purely gratuitous gift made solely out of natural love and affection without receiving anything in return. Enjoys full tax concessions among eligible relatives.
  • Heba-bil-Ewaz (হেবা-বিল-এওয়াজ): A gift made in return for an express consideration or reciprocal gift (e.g., in consideration of gold, prayer mat, Quran, or monetary sum). Under Bangladeshi law, Heba-bil-Ewaz is treated for tax purposes similarly to a sale; unless executed among the same 33 close blood relations, it attracts standard registration duty and local taxes.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Procedure to Execute a Heba Deed from Abroad
sections.content:
If the donor lives in New York, London, Toronto, etc., follow this roadmap:

  1. Draft a Special Power of Attorney for Heba Execution in Form 1 specifying the property schedule and identifying the donee.
  2. Attend the Bangladesh Embassy / High Commission in the USA, UK, or Canada for consular signature and attestation.
  3. Send the deed to Bangladesh for MOFA authentication and DC office stamp duty adjudication.
  4. The engaged Attorney attends the Sub-Registry Office in Bangladesh with the donee to execute and register the final Heba Deed (হেবা দলিল).
  5. Immediately apply online for e-Namjari mutation at mutation.land.gov.bd to record the donee's name in the government record-of-rights.

sections.h2: Government Fees & Tax Comparison: Heba vs Sale Deed
sections.content:
Executing a Heba saves tremendous financial capital compared to a sale deed (সাফ কবলা):

  • Sale Deed: Stamp Duty (1.5-3%), Registration Fee (1%), Local Govt Tax (2-3%), Advance Source Tax (2-8%), AIT = Total 8% to 15% of property value.
  • Heba Deed (Between 33 Relations): Stamp Duty = BDT 100, Registration Fee = BDT 100, Local Govt Tax = Exempted in most categories, Minimal N-fee & E-fee = Total under BDT 5,000–10,000 regardless of property value!

sections.h2: Can a Registered Heba Deed Be Cancelled Later?
sections.content:
A common concern is whether a donor can unilaterally revoke a Heba after a family dispute:

Under Muslim law and Section 126 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882, a Heba made between close blood relations (e.g., parent to child, husband to wife) becomes completely irrevocable once delivery of possession and registration are complete. The donor CANNOT unilaterally execute a cancellation deed (বাতিল দলিল) at the Sub-Registry. Any cancellation requires a formal civil court decree based on proven fraud or coercion.

faqs.question: Can I gift a flat in Dhaka to my daughter living with me in the UK?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can execute a Power of Attorney at the Bangladesh High Commission in London to register the Heba deed in Dhaka, transferring full title to your daughter with BDT 100 stamp duty.

faqs.question: Do I have to pay capital gains tax on a Heba gift in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: No. Gifting property between eligible close blood relations is exempt from capital gains tax and advance source tax under the Income Tax Act 2023.

faqs.question: Can I give a Heba to my cousin or sister-in-law under the BDT 100 fee rule?
faqs.answer: No. Cousins and in-laws fall outside the 33 designated blood relations. Gifting to them is treated as a general gift, attracting standard stamp duty and local registration taxes.

faqs.question: Is physical delivery of possession possible if both donor and donee reside abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes. Constructive delivery of possession (such as handing over original title deeds, transferring rent collection authority, or instructing the caretaker) is fully recognized in law.

faqs.question: What is the timeline to complete an e-Namjari mutation after a Heba deed?
faqs.answer: An online e-Namjari mutation typically takes 28 working days through the Assistant Commissioner (Land) office once the registered Heba deed is issued.
